summary: CLD v2 denotes the July 2025 paper version, not ordinal stage 2. Checked ordinary approximation gives stage 1 for LFS and stage 2 for interior semipositive real PL; GJR curve regularization supplies weakly smooth nets and needs additional arguments.
detailedSummary: CD Definition 8.1.1 and Lemma 8.1.4 use ordinary smooth positive functions and decreasing sequences. GJR 15.11 requires a boundaryless rig-smooth curve and gives a decreasing net of weakly smooth psh functions. Its Remark 15.10 identifies these with ordinary smooth functions under a residue-field or local-genus hypothesis. GJR 7.10 requires an interior point; its common-neighborhood uniform LFS approximation safely yields ordinal stage 2 for semipositive real PL, without flattening the two approximation operations.
text:
These are checked published foundations and fresh stage bookkeeping. CD denotes the supplied arXiv:1204.6277v2 PDF, dated 25 July 2025. Definition 8.1.1 (p.195) defines the smallest subsheaf containing ordinary smooth q with d'd''q≥0 and closed under decreasing sequences. Lemma 8.1.4 (p.196) defines Psh_0 as those smooth functions, Psh_{α+1} by local decreasing sequential limits of Psh_α, and limit stages by local membership in earlier stages. Thus paper version v2 and ordinal stage 2 are distinct. Current positivity or classical pshness does not alone establish membership in a specified ordinal stage.

CD 12.4.1/12.4.6 supplies the canonical refined analytic G-tropical structure. CD 15.1.1(b)/15.1.2 describes ordinary smooth functions through ordinary open local expressions φ(-log|g_1|,…,-log|g_r|), with analytic units and smooth φ. G-local real PL and harmonic tropicalizations cannot replace this ordinary smoothness. CD 15.7.1 associates the tropical structure to a Hausdorff pure-dimensional analytic space with its actual analytic boundary; 15.7.2 records the boundary formula for domains. CD 12.4.5 and 8.1.5 preserve each ordinal stage under analytic morphisms, including scalar projections between different complete fields. On boundaryless tropical spaces, CD 8.3.1(b) converts current positivity into positive d'd'' forms for ordinary smooth functions.

GJR denotes the supplied arXiv:2111.05741. Definition 5.1 defines real PL using G-local real combinations of unit log norms. Definition 7.8 and 7.9 make LFS a semipositive real-PL class and supply ordinary local expressions as nonnegative combinations of finite maxima of negative log norms of analytic units. For each maximum, on its fixed ordinary neighborhood, use M_ε=ε log Σ exp(ℓ_i/ε). It satisfies 0≤M_ε−max ℓ_i≤ε log N, has positive Hessian, and ∂M_ε/∂ε=−Σp_i log p_i≥0. Consequently ε↓0 gives a decreasing ordinary smooth positive sequence. Finite nonnegative combinations preserve this construction. Thus LFS functions belong locally to Psh_1.

GJR Proposition 7.10 (pp.47–48) requires an interior point. Its proof produces a common ordinary open tube U=red^{-1}(V') and LFS h_i converging uniformly to a semipositive real-PL h. Choose ||h_{i_j}−h||_U≤e_j=4^{-j} and set b_j=h_{i_j}+2e_j. Then h+e_j≤b_j≤h+3e_j and b_{j+1}≤h+3e_{j+1}<h+e_j≤b_j. Each b_j belongs to stage 1, so b_j↓h proves stage 2. Each inner smooth sequence has a fixed ordinary neighborhood; the outer sequence is defined on U. A single smooth sequence on U approximating h is not proved by this argument.

GJR Proposition 15.11 (pp.80–81) explicitly assumes a smooth curve, meaning rig-smooth without boundary. It produces a decreasing net of weakly smooth psh functions on any relatively compact ordinary open subset. Remark 15.10 identifies weak and ordinary smooth sheaves when the residue field is algebraic over a finite field, or the curve is potentially locally P1. Remark 10.10 identifies its ordinary smooth sheaf with the CLD ordinary sheaf. After this identification, positive weak currents restrict to positive ordinary currents, and CD 8.3.1(b) gives stage-0 form positivity. Outside these cases harmonic germs can be non-smooth; this is not proof that stage 1 or 2 fails.

Further checked foundations are GRc=arXiv:2506.13548v2, 17 September 2025: Theorem 4.3 identifies semipositive real PL with classical psh on good strict spaces over nontrivially valued fields; Definition 4.1 quantifies over every analytic extension and curve morphism; Lemma 3.9 describes normalization over perfect fields; Theorems 6.1 and 6.4 give interior and Shilov maximum principles. In the supplied arXiv:2503.05513, the curve subharmonic real-PL/nef equivalence is Proposition 5.1, despite GRc's older cross-citation to Proposition 3.1. Thuillier Proposition 3.1.8(iii), printed p.62/PDF p.76, concerns increasing locally bounded subharmonic families. His Theorem 3.4.2 supplies decreasing families of subharmonic lisse functions, and Proposition 3.2.5 identifies these as G-local real PL, not ordinary CLD-smooth.

All six supplied PDF/text hash pairs matched. Seventy-five literal primary pages, including indispensable proof continuations, are retained in source-extracts/source-provenance.json. Actual PDF pages Thu 76, CD 196 and GJR 80 were visually inspected. Thu actually says 'famille croissante et localement bornée'; GJR actually says 'decreasing net', 'weakly smooth', and 'without boundary'. Run python extract_sources.py and python render_sources.py. Renderer diagnostics are retained, including Thu's Type-3 glyph warnings. Hashes and rendering success are provenance evidence, not mathematical proof certificates.

summary: Full-union envelopes have ordinary CLD stage 1 on boundaryless reduced good strict pure curves with bijective normalization over perfect countably dense fields whose residue is algebraic over a finite field. This includes positive-genus curves over Qp. Without the residue/genus hypothesis the checked route gives only stage 3.
detailedSummary: For every usc obstacle, finite maxima containing a baseline make the entire normalized competitor family locally bounded on both sides. Thuillier's supremum theorem gives a subharmonic regularized envelope. Countable local topology extracts a sequence from a decreasing continuous net on a fixed ordinary neighborhood. Under the residue hypothesis, GJR's approximants are ordinary smooth, yielding stage 1. They descend through homeomorphic normalization because ordinary smooth functions are locally constant at rigid points. All analytic extensions and curve pullbacks preserve the bound. Without ordinary/weak sheaf equality, the real-PL regularization and stage-2 approximation lemma yield stage 3, not stage 2.
text:
Theorem. Let K be complete, nontrivially valued and perfect, with a countable dense subset. Let X be a nonempty reduced, separated, good, strictly K-analytic curve pure of dimension one, with ∂X=∅ and normalization ν:X̃→X bijective on Berkovich points. If the residue field K̃ is algebraic over a finite field, then for EVERY usc f:X→R∪{−∞}, the usc regularization u of the supremum over the FULL real-valued locally-Fubini–Study/semipositive-real-PL minorant union belongs to Psh_{X,1}⊂Psh_{X,2}. At every point it is a decreasing sequence of finite ordinary CLD-smooth functions with positive d'd'' on one ordinary neighborhood. The same conclusion holds under the alternative hypothesis that X̃ is potentially locally P1. Without either residue/genus hypothesis, the proof below establishes only Psh_{X,3}.

Full-family supremum step. If the family is empty, both envelopes are −∞, approximated by the smooth constants −j. Otherwise choose one competitor h_0. Every competitor is finite continuous and classically psh by n1. Therefore f is finite everywhere and locally upper bounded. Also h_0≤s≤u≤f, the last inequality following from usc of f. GRc Lemma 3.9 makes X̃ rig-smooth and boundaryless. Since ν is a bijective topological quotient, it is a homeomorphism. Pull back the entire family, direct finite subsets containing h_0 by inclusion, and take their maxima. These are subharmonic and locally bounded below by h_0∘ν and above by f∘ν. They need not be real PL; no real-PL maximum closure is assumed. Thuillier 3.1.8(iii) makes (s∘ν)* subharmonic. Homeomorphic regularization gives (s∘ν)*=u∘ν. This treats the entire family without a modulus or invariance restriction.

Sequence extraction. A strict K-affinoid algebra is separable as a Banach space because countably many Tate polynomials with coefficients in a countable dense subset of K have dense images. The inequality | |a(x)|−|b(x)| |≤||a−b|| shows that countably many evaluations generate the topology and separate points of its spectrum. The compact spectrum embeds in a countable product of compact real intervals, hence is second countable. A relatively compact ordinary open W in a good Hausdorff space is covered by finitely many interiors of affinoid neighborhoods of its compact closure, so is second countable. For a decreasing directed net a_i of continuous functions with infimum v on W, {v<t}=⋃_i{a_i<t} is open and Lindelof. Choose a countable subcover for each rational t, enumerate all chosen indices, and successively take dominating indices. This gives a decreasing sequence on the SAME W. If its limit exceeded v at a point, an intermediate rational threshold and its chosen covering index would contradict that inequality. Thus the sequence converges to v, including where v=−∞.

Stage 1. On a relatively compact ordinary neighborhood W̃ in X̃, GJR 15.11 gives a decreasing net of finite weakly smooth psh functions converging to u∘ν. The residue hypothesis, or the stated potentially-local-P1 hypothesis, makes these ordinary smooth by GJR 15.10. Their positive ordinary currents give positive ordinary forms by CD 8.3.1(b), so they are stage 0. Extract an actual decreasing sequence on W̃.

Ordinary smooth descent. Normalization is an analytic isomorphism off a discrete set of non-normal rigid points. An ordinary smooth function is locally constant at a rigid point, including one with a finite residue extension. To prove this, let g be an analytic unit at such a point z, α=g(z), ρ=|α|>0, and P its monic minimal polynomial of degree d. All conjugate roots have modulus ρ because K is complete. On the ordinary neighborhood |P(g)|<ρ^d, if |g(y)|≠ρ then, after algebraic extension of H(y), every root difference has modulus max(|g(y)|,ρ), giving |P(g(y))|≥ρ^d, a contradiction. Hence |g| is constant there. Apply this to the finitely many units in an ordinary smooth moment expression. Transfer each normalized approximant through the homeomorphism. Away from non-normal points it is smooth and positive by analytic isomorphism; at those points it is constant on an ordinary neighborhood, hence smooth with zero d'd''. Thus the transferred functions are stage 0 on W=ν(W̃), and decrease to u. This proves stage 1. Induction gives the same descent for the finite ordinal stages used below.

General residue fields. Thuillier 3.4.2 supplies a decreasing net of continuous subharmonic lisse functions on W̃. They are real PL by Proposition 3.2.5 and semipositive by the supplied GRs Proposition 5.1. The interior lemma in n1 places each in stage 2. Extracting a decreasing sequence gives stage 3; descent gives Psh_{X,3}. No collapse to stage 2 is justified.

Scalar and curve quantifiers. For EVERY complete analytic extension K'/K and analytic curve morphism g:C→X_{K'}, CD 12.4.5/8.1.5 preserves the proved ordinal bound for u∘π∘g. The ordinary smooth sequences and all their decreasing limits pull back. Smooth psh curve functions are subharmonic, and decreasing limits remain so, as checked in GRc §1.2 and Proposition 3.5. This also gives scalar-stable classical pshness, including −∞ in the extended convention. Neither openness of scalar projection nor equality of envelopes for enlarged scalar-extension competitor families is asserted or needed.

This is a noninvariant full-family sector covering boundaryless ordinary open domains in smooth elliptic and higher-genus curves over Qp. It is not a rational-tree example or selected invariant family. Continuity is not asserted. The sufficient field hypotheses are not shown necessary; relative-boundary points and arbitrary imperfect perfected-unibranch descent remain unresolved.

summary: Every noninvariant full-union obstacle envelope on an ordinary locally trivial projective-space bundle reduces exactly to a base envelope. The curve sector in n2 therefore gives ordinary stage 1 in higher dimension.
detailedSummary: Every competitor is constant on compact connected projective fibers by the scalar-stable classical maximum principle. Ordinary local sections descend both competitor branches, and pullback gives the converse. For any usc obstacle F, its fiberwise infimum g is usc because the smooth bundle projection is open. Raw envelopes and their regularizations are exact pullbacks, including empty families. The stage-1 curve sector and its broader stage-3 counterpart propagate through projective factors and finite bundle towers. The exact reduction permits base boundary, but supplies no missing positive boundary theorem.
text:
Exact reduction theorem. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued. Let X be any good separated strict K-analytic space, allowing relative boundary. Let p:Y→X be a good separated projective-space bundle locally analytically trivial on ORDINARY open subsets, with fiber P^{m,an}, m≥1. For every usc F:Y→R∪{−∞}, put g(x)=inf_{p^{-1}(x)}F. Then g is usc, and for the FULL LFS/semipositive-real-PL union, s_F^Y=s_g^X∘p and (s_F^Y)*=(s_g^X)*∘p, including empty families.

Proof. Every competitor h is finite continuous and classically psh by n1. Restrict it to the fiber over x, viewed as analytic projective space over H(x), using scalar extension and analytic pullback. This fiber is compact, connected and boundaryless. Connectedness follows from its m+1 standard closed unit-polydisc domains: each is connected because a clopen partition would glue a nontrivial analytic idempotent into its Tate algebra, which is a domain; all contain (1:…:1). They cover projective space by choosing a largest homogeneous coordinate. The restriction of h attains a maximum. Its maximum set is closed by continuity and open by GRc's interior local maximum principle. Connectedness makes it the whole fiber. Thus EVERY competitor is fiberwise constant, without a symmetry assumption.

Write h=b∘p. On each ordinary trivializing open, restrict h along the analytic section (1:0:…:0). LFS expressions pull back to LFS expressions; GJR 5.4/7.6 preserves real PL and semipositivity for the other branch. These local functions agree by fiberwise constancy and give a global b in the same branch. Conversely p*b preserves either branch. This is an exact correspondence, and h≤F is equivalent to b≤g.

The projection p is smooth and surjective, hence open by Berkovich's supplied IHES 1993 paper, Corollary 3.7.4, applied to its ordinary local projective-space trivializations and relative affine charts. Therefore {g<t}=p({F<t}) is open for each real t, proving usc. The argument allows g=−∞, even when F is pointwise finite. The competitor correspondence proves raw equality, including empty families.

For a continuous open surjection p and raw extended function a, (a∘p)*=a*∘p. Continuity gives the upper inequality by pulling back base neighborhoods. Openness gives the lower inequality because the image of every neighborhood of a chosen lift is a base neighborhood. The neighborhood-supremum formula works also at −∞. Applying it to the raw identity proves regularized equality.

If X satisfies n2's residue-field curve theorem, every full envelope on Y belongs to ordinary stage 1, hence stage 2: pull back the actual decreasing smooth sequence for the usc obstacle g. Its members are ordinary smooth and positive on the common ordinary neighborhood p^{-1}(W), and decrease to the actual full envelope. All analytic extensions and curve tests preserve this bound. If only n2's broader curve hypotheses hold, the proved bound is stage 3. Finite towers follow by repetition because each effective obstacle remains usc. Products X×P^{m,an} are included; normal curve bases give normal higher-dimensional spaces.

The positive conclusion uses a boundaryless base from n2; the total space is boundaryless because the projection is boundaryless. The exact reduction itself allows a base boundary and does not manufacture a curve boundary-approximation theorem. Arbitrary normal domains, open-disc products and general proper fibrations without ordinary local sections remain outside this sector. All noninvariant obstacles and competitors are admitted; proper fibers force descent rather than selecting an invariant subfamily.

detailedSummary: On Z=M(K〈x,y〉/(xy)), set a=−log|π|>0, r=|π|, and take obstacle 0 on the x-branch and −a min(|y|/r,1) on the y-branch. The radius-r disc maximum principle bounds every competitor by −a on the y-branch. Explicit LFS minorants show the exact raw envelope is 0 on the punctured x-branch and −a elsewhere. Regularization raises the node to 0, violating the y-disc Shilov maximum principle and every CLD ordinal stage. This works on Int(Z) and propagates through projective factors. It does not establish sharp necessity or resolve broader normal geometry. Deliverables, source extracts and two successful TeX builds are retained; candidate is false.
text:
Fresh counterexample with a complete full-family calculation. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, choose π with 0<|π|<1, and put a=−log|π|>0 and r=|π|. Let Z=M(K〈x,y〉/(xy)), with node o and branches D_x,D_y. Let V be either Z or its boundaryless interior Int(Z), whose branches are open unit discs joined at o. Define f=0 on D_x∩V and f=−a min(|y|/r,1) on D_y∩V. Both branch values equal 0 at o, so f is finite continuous by nodal gluing.

Every member h of the FULL LFS/semipositive-real-PL minorant union restricts to a classically psh function on the closed y-disc of radius r. This strict affinoid disc lies inside either V. Its singleton Shilov point η_r satisfies h(η_r)≤f(η_r)=−a. The Gauss seminorm dominates every point seminorm on each analytic power series, verifying its Shilov property. GRc Theorem 6.4 gives h≤−a throughout the disc, including o. Outside it, f is already −a. Thus all competitors are ≤−a on the entire y-branch.

Define h_n=max(−a,n^{-1}log|x|) on the x-branch and h_n=−a on the y-branch, giving o value −a. These are finite continuous LFS functions. On a nodal neighborhood with both branch radii <|π|^n they are constant. Away from o on the x-branch, x is a unit and h_n=n^{-1}max{−log|π^{-n}|,−log|x^{-1}|}, an ordinary local LFS expression. On the y-branch they are constant. They satisfy h_n≤f. At every punctured x-branch point log|x| is finite and h_n→0, while f gives the upper bound 0. On the y-branch they attain the established upper bound −a. Hence the exact raw envelope is s=0 on (D_x∩V)\{o} and s=−a on D_y∩V, including o.

Usc regularization changes only o to value 0. Its pullback to the closed y-disc has value 0 at the origin and −a at the singleton Shilov point, contradicting the psh maximum principle. It is not classically psh and belongs to no CLD ordinal psh stage: ordinary smooth curve psh functions are subharmonic, decreasing limits preserve subharmonicity, and the transfinite local construction preserves the scalar-stable classical class. This branch obstruction already occurs without relative boundary when V=Int(Z); choosing V=Z also checks the affinoid-boundary setting.

For V×P^{m,an} with obstacle f∘p, n3's exact reduction gives the regularized envelope u∘p. A projective-space section and the same closed y-disc witness failure in dimension m+1 for every m≥1. No dossier book assertion, earlier generated counterexample or review verdict is used.

Original obligations remain open. The sectors in n2 and n3 are sufficient, not a sharp classification. Necessity of residue-field, countability and boundarylessness assumptions is not proved. Non-smooth harmonic germs do not imply absence from stage 1 or 2. The broader curve construction reaches stage 3, and reducing it to ordinal stage 2 needs another ordinary approximation argument. Imperfect perfected-unibranch descent, positive approximation at relative-boundary points, arbitrary normal/geometrically-unibranch higher-dimensional domains and open-disc products are unresolved. No fresh proof is supplied for the dossier's nonsplit-node surface or codimension-two pinching assertions, and they were not imported. Scalar pullback positivity of every proved envelope is established, but enlarged scalar competitor-family identities are not asserted. No continuity or P03.1/P03.3 classification is claimed. Therefore the original sharp P03.2 target remains open and candidate=false.
